title: 'Best Targets Tonight' ranks purely by transit altitude, so it recommends obscure galaxies that transit in daylight and pass through the zenith
repairSummary: Made the panel's disclosed rule match the key it actually sorts by. Named the blend weights (kTonightConditionsWeight = 0.7 / kTonightCatalogFitWeight = 0.3) in packages/skotiq_planetarium/lib/src/planning/tonight_ranking.dart, replaced the two magic literals in rankTonightTargets with them, and derived a single kTonightRankingTooltip string FROM those constants so the words cannot drift from the weights again. tonight_tab.dart:315 now renders that constant instead of the hand-written 'the same score the planner uses' prose. Corrected two doc comments that also claimed the field was the planner's night score (TonightRanking.score and TonightTarget.score). Two new tests: tonight_ranking_test.dart 'catalog fit can outrank a clearly better night score' pins the divergence with real numbers (asserts TargetScoringService prefers index 0 while the panel returns index 1 first, WITH fewer usable dark hours than the row under it) and 'the tooltip states that rule instead of claiming planner parity' pins the disclosure to the constants; tonight_tab_dark_hours_test.dart 'the header tooltip is the ranker's own disclosed rule' fails if the widget goes back to hand-written prose. No ranking behaviour was changed - the blend is deliberate and test-covered, so removing it would have re-opened the 'obscure galaxies' half of the finding.
reasoning: The behavioural cause IS fixed and wired: packages/skotiq_planetarium/lib/src/planning/tonight_ranking.dart exists with darknessWindowOf() degrading astronomical -> nautical -> civil -> sunset and returning null under a midnight sun, targets with hoursAboveMinAlt <= 0 inside the window are dropped, and survivors are scored with TargetScoringService.scoreTargetForNight over [window.start, window.end] at minAltitude 30 (verified in target_scoring.dart:320-460 that hoursAboveMinAlt and peakAltitudeTime are both measured INSIDE the passed window). Both consumer surfaces read bestTargetsProvider (desktop tonight_tab.dart:109, mobile mobile_widgets/search_sheet.dart:160) and the mobile one prints no metric at all, so there is no unfixed copy. What does NOT hold is the fix's own claim, repeated verbatim to the operator. The summary says 'No new weighting was invented... so the panel can no longer call a target best on a key the planner and the native scheduler disagree with', and the shipped tooltip said 'the same score the planner uses'. Both are false: tonight_ranking.dart:203 (pre-repair) sorted on `score.totalScore * 0.7 + catalogQuality * 0.3` where _catalogQualityScore is a brand-new magnitude / size-vs-FOV / object-type axis TargetScoringService has never had, and it is not a tie-break - I measured it. This is the cry-wolf shape this campaign is chasing, and it is operator-visible on the same card: the top row can show FEWER usable dark hours than the row beneath it while a tooltip says the list is ranked on usable hours. Behaviour fixed, stated rule not; hence INCOMPLETE rather than HOLDS or RELOCATED.
evidence: Divergence measured, not inferred. Probe at 40N/105W on the night of 2026-08-02 with two targets - A: transits mid-darkness at dec=+40, mag 14.5; B: 20 min after dusk at dec=0, mag 5.0 - gave panel order [B blended 84.27 (3.75 usable dark hours), A blended 72.38 (6.25 hours)] while the app's own TargetScoringService.scoreTargetForNight over the same window gave [A 87.33, B 83.95]. So the panel's first row had the LOWER planner score AND 2.5 fewer usable hours than the row it outranked, under a tooltip claiming parity with the planner and a subtitle headlining those hours. That probe is now a shipped test. Severance of the production wiring: replaced the body of _rankTonightTargetsOffThread (mosaic_targets.dart) with `return const []`; tonight_ranking_provider_wiring_test.dart went 3 green -> 1 pass / 2 RED ('the card itself, not just the ranker, refuses a daylight culmination' -> Expected non-empty, Actual []; 'active equipment FOV reaches the isolate ranking inputs' -> Bad state: No element). File restored and byte-compared identical to the pre-severance copy. Noted but not repaired: the third wiring test, 'every target the card offers has dark hours and a dark peak', passes VACUOUSLY on an empty list - it is a forall with no non-empty guard. Also confirmed _currentNightDateProvider (catalog_astronomy.dart:153) truncates through nightDateOf to a bare date, so the ~6.4 s isolate job is not re-triggered per minute.

title: Search hint badge reads '⌘K' on Linux and Windows, where the shortcut is Ctrl+K
repairSummary: Test-robustness only, no behaviour change. The command bar was the one call site with no platform-explicit pin: its only coverage was search_command_focus_test.dart:117 locating the control via find.text(shortcutLabel('K')), which is a tautology on any macOS runner (flutter_test does NOT force a target platform - I checked the SDK, there is no debugDefaultTargetPlatformOverride default in packages/flutter_test/lib/src/binding.dart - so defaultTargetPlatform is the host, and a hardcoded '⌘K' would still be found on a Mac). Added 'the command bar badge is platform-derived too' to search_shortcut_badge_platform_test.dart: it pumps PlanetariumCommandBar under an explicit TargetPlatform.linux override, asserts 'Ctrl+K' is present and the glyph absent, and asserts no exception (the wider label must not overflow the fixed 200px search chip). Verified it goes RED when the badge is hardcoded back. dart format run.
reasoning: The claim is true at code level and, unusually for a label fix, the label it now prints is actually correct. packages/skotiq_ui/lib/src/utils/platform_shortcuts.dart exists with shortcutModifierLabel()/shortcutLabel(key) switching on defaultTargetPlatform, is exported from the skotiq_ui barrel, and is used at BOTH claimed sites (redesign/command_bar.dart:198, search_header.dart:670). I checked the premise rather than trusting it: the handler at packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/planetarium/planetarium_screen/actions.dart:512 fires on LogicalKeyboardKey.keyK with isMetaPressed OR isControlPressed, so 'Ctrl+K' on Linux/Windows is a key that genuinely works - this is not a DISCLOSURE-ONLY relabel of a broken binding, and not INVERTED. A repo-wide grep for the Command glyph across packages/*/lib and apps/*/lib returns zero production occurrences (only doc comments and test expectations), and a grep for other Apple modifier glyphs (⌥ ⇧ ⌃) and for 'Cmd+'/'Meta+' literals returns nothing, so there is no third badge. Layout checked by hand as well as by test: the command-bar chip is a fixed 200x32 Row whose 'Search' label is the Expanded child, leaving ~114px for a ~42px label, and the header badge is an InputDecoration suffixIcon that sizes to its content.
evidence: Severance A (search_header.dart:670): replaced shortcutLabel('K') with a literal '\u2318K'; search_shortcut_badge_platform_test.dart went 4 green -> 2 pass / 2 RED (the Linux and Windows cases). Severance B (redesign/command_bar.dart:198): same substitution; search_command_focus_test.dart went 3 green -> 3 RED (all three tests locate the Search control by that text). Both files restored and grep-confirmed clean of the marker. Scope note, deliberately NOT edited because it is another area's files: the same defect class exists INVERTED across the sequencer, which hardcodes 'Ctrl+' in operator-facing strings on every platform - sequencer_screen_parts/tab_bar.dart:221-226 (the shortcut cheat sheet), sequence_toolbar.dart:552/557 ('Undo (Ctrl+Z)'), toolbox_panel.dart:129, delete_node_confirmation.dart:74/77, batch_operations_toolbar.dart:223/226, templates_tab_parts/_header_and_filters.dart:52 - so a macOS operator is told to press Ctrl there. shortcutLabel() is now available to fix it; it belongs to the sequencer shard, not this one.

title: Object search has no exact-designation path: typing a catalogue number returns 175 fuzzy matches
repairSummary: Test-fidelity only, no behaviour change. The star half of the fix was covered by a fixture the shipped loader cannot produce: search_designation_ranking_test.dart used a star with zero-padded ids ('HD006720', catalogIds ['HD 006720','HIP 005300']) and a comment asserting 'a star's catalogue ids are zero-padded in HYG exactly as the DSO cross-identifiers are'. That is false - packages/skotiq_planetarium/lib/src/catalogs/star_catalog.dart:296-332 builds ids as `HIP$n`/`HD$n` and cross-ids as `HIP $n`/`HD $n` with NO padding. Corrected the comment to say which shape is which and added 'an UNPADDED HYG-shaped star id is an exact designation too', which uses the real emitted shape and a BRIGHTER decoy DSO whose commonNames is exactly 'HIP 5300' (so both sit at _scoreMatch band 0 and the magnitude tie-break hands the decoy the top slot unless the designation branch lifts the star to -1). Verified RED when the star branch is deleted, for both queries ('HIP 5300' and 'hip5300'). dart format run.
reasoning: Everything the summary describes is in the file and behaves as claimed. _splitDesignation (object_search.dart:195) normalises whitespace/underscores and strips zero padding via ^([a-z]*)0*(\d+)$, returning null for composite survey ids; _isExactDesignation pins the catalogue for a prefixed query and gates a bare number to _bareNumberCatalogs = {m, ngc, ic}; _exactDesignationScore = -1 sits below _scoreMatch's exact band of 0. It is applied in BOTH loops - the star loop short-circuits with `continue` (416-429), the DSO loop applies it last and unconditionally so it overrides every fuzzier band (583-590). I checked the data claim against the real asset rather than the summary: packages/skotiq_planetarium/assets/opengnc/NGC.csv genuinely carries 'PGC 067202' on IC5118, 'UGC 06720' on IC728 and 'PGC 067209' on NGC7107, and the Messier number is appended to catalogIds (catalog.dart:205-207) so 'M57' resolves NGC6720 through the designation path too. The stated narrowing is real and not a swap of one wrong answer for another: a bare number cannot reach an HD star, and 'UGC 6720' cannot answer NGC6720. Recorded residual, deliberately NOT repaired: the fix is ranking-only, so the finding's LITERAL symptom persists - I measured 166 results for '6720' over a HYG-sized (120k) star list, and search_header.dart:245 says in so many words 'Show all results grouped by category, no hardcoded limit'. Suppressing the substring band for designation-shaped queries would cut that list, but it would also DELETE the star a user typing '6720' might have wanted (HD 6720 reaches the list only through that band), which is the INVERTED failure this review is supposed to catch - so it is a product decision, not a defect I should force. The operator-visible failure named in the finding - a first result that was right only by luck of the brightness tie-break, and a wrong Enter/fly-to - is genuinely cured.
evidence: Severance A (DSO loop, object_search.dart:583-590): deleted the block; search_designation_ranking_test.dart + search_resolver_test.dart went 14 green -> 4 RED, including '"m31", "andromeda galaxy" and "NGC224" resolve to the same object'. Severance B (star loop, 416-429): deleted the block; 'a padded star catalogue id is an exact designation too' RED with Expected HD006720 / Actual NGC9999, and my new HYG-shaped test RED as well. File restored and diff-confirmed byte-identical after each experiment. Performance checked because the branch adds up to 4 _splitDesignation calls (2 RegExp allocations each) per star: over a synthetic 120k-star catalog a designation query ('6720') took 1060 ms versus 1189 ms for a plain word query ('rigelx'), so the new branch is not a search-latency regression - the ~1 s cost is the pre-existing full-catalog scan, which the UI debounces by 250 ms (search_header.dart:111). Confirmed there is no unfixed second search surface: every planetarium entry point - search_header, search_tab, mobile_widgets/search_sheet, planetarium_shell, layouts.dart, actions.dart - goes through objectSearchProvider, and Enter/fly-to goes through resolveBest, which returns results.first.

title: Region detail opens on a viewport-filling empty preview with no empty state; everything informative is below the fold
reasoning: Both cause fixes are present, load-bearing, and correctly scoped. region_detail_screen.dart:219-243 replaces the free AspectRatio with a LayoutBuilder sizing the hero to math.min(constraints.maxWidth * 2/3, _kCutoutMaxHeight) inside a SizedBox, with _kCutoutMaxHeight = 320 at line 295 and BoxFit.cover on the cutout; _EmptyCutout (311-348) renders 'Nothing imaged here yet' plus 'Point a session at this patch of sky and its frames fold in here.' inside the preview. Crucially the cap sits OUTSIDE the empty/non-empty branch, so the below-the-fold half of the finding is fixed on every path, not just the one the fixer tested. The growth-card change is confined to the caller: atlas_growth_curve.dart:181 swaps AdaptiveChartContainer.fixed(height: 170) for ConstrainedBox(minHeight: 170) at that one placeholder, and git status shows the shared analytics/widgets/adaptive_chart_container.dart is untouched, so no other screen's chart geometry moved. Checked for the missed-fourth-surface this campaign keeps producing: the only other AtlasRegionCutout hero is atlas_region_card.dart:45, which already had its own _PreviewPlaceholder and is bounded by a 16:9 AspectRatio inside a grid cell, so it never had either half of this defect. Residual recorded rather than repaired, because it is a state the finding did not name: when a region HAS folds but the cutout PNG is missing or the fetch fails, AtlasRegionCutout falls through to _CutoutState, which is still a bare surfaceAlt box with a single imageOff glyph and no words. I reproduced it. It is now capped at 320px instead of filling the viewport, and the surrounding screen already says 'Reconnect to your imaging host to export this co-add.' on that path, so the operator is not left guessing - and adding copy to _CutoutState would also change the small grid-cell preview, which is shared with the card. Flagging, not editing.
evidence: Severance A (the words): replaced _EmptyCutout with a plain Container(color: colors.surfaceAlt); BOTH tests in region_detail_empty_state_test.dart went RED with 'Found 0 widgets with text "Nothing imaged here yet"'. Severance B (the cap): dropped the math.min so the hero is free again; 'an empty region says so inside the preview, and its facts stay on a 1600x900 screen' failed with 'Expected: a value less than <430> / Actual: <1126.33>', which independently reproduces the fixer's claimed ~1030px hero (1552 * 2/3 plus the card chrome). File restored and diff-confirmed byte-identical after each. Residual reproduced with a throwaway probe: a region with one SkyAtlasFoldRow and atlasRegionCutoutProvider throwing renders the screen with the coordinate line, 'Contributing frames', the fold row and the growth placeholder all present, and 'Nothing imaged here yet' absent - i.e. a wordless hero. Probe deleted. Regression sweep after all of my edits: skotiq_app test/screens/planetarium + test/screens/your_sky + observing_site_gating_test.dart = 197 passed; skotiq_planetarium full suite = 506 passed, 1 failed (see regressionsFound).
